scenes.title: What Is Turbulence?
scenes.text: Sometimes, the plane suddenly shakes and bumps. That's turbulence! But what is it, and should you worry?

scenes.title: What It Feels Like
scenes.text: What does turbulence feel like? A bit like a car on a bumpy road, or a boat on little waves. The plane rises and dips a tiny bit, but it stays right on course.

scenes.title: A River of Air
scenes.text: Air flows like an invisible river. When the river is smooth, the ride is smooth. But when the air swirls and tumbles, like water rushing over rocks, the plane gets bumped around.

scenes.title: Where Bumps Come From
scenes.text: Bumpy air comes from many things: warm air rising from the sunny ground, wind tumbling over mountains, and big, puffy storm clouds.

scenes.title: Hidden Bumps
scenes.text: Some bumps hide in clear blue sky, where very fast winds called jet streams rub against slower air. Pilots radio reports to each other, so other planes can steer around the bumpy spots.

scenes.title: Built Tough
scenes.text: But don't worry! Airplanes are built super strong. Their wings can bend and flex, like a bird's, and they're tested far beyond the biggest bumps they'll ever meet.

scenes.title: Staying Safe
scenes.text: Pilots use weather radar to steer around storms. And when it might get bumpy, they switch on the seatbelt sign. So keep your seatbelt fastened, and enjoy the ride!

scenes.title: Remember!
scenes.text: Rivers of air, rising heat, mountains, storms and jet streams, strong wings, and seatbelts on. That's turbulence! See you on the next flight.
